title: Guest conflict and L.E.A.R.N.
lead: How to turn a complaint around, and what to do for the issues that come up most. Always notify a manager.

sections.name: The L.E.A.R.N. method
know: Empathize validate how the guest feels.
Resolve with a plan the guest agrees to.
Note report it to your supervisor, even if it’s fixed.

items.name: Resolve
items.text: a plan the guest agrees to

sections.name: Waits, wrong orders and spoiled food

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Apologize, fix it, bring in a manager.

know: Thank them for their patience when the wait runs long.
Replace a wrong order with the right one, right away.
Comp it spoiled or inedible food, and replace it.
The line managers inspect it after spoiled food.

sections.name: Spills, dirty tables and poor service

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Show genuine care, then get help.

know: Towels dry and wet, right away, after a spill.
Thank them for pointing out a dirty table or restroom.
Support team takes the cleanup if you’re mid-service.
Manager steps in when a guest reports poor service.

keyPoints.line: with a plan the guest agrees to.
report it to your supervisor, even if it’s fixed.

read.where: An unhappy guest can **significantly damage** a restaurant’s reputation, while a successfully resolved complaint can build **lifelong loyalty**. **Sincerity and urgency** are critical. With every complaint, **always notify a manager**.

stops.name: Listen
stops.text: Stay **calm and composed**, and listen carefully to the complaint **without interrupting**. Avoid matching aggressive energy.

stops.name: Empathize
stops.text: Show **sincere concern** and validate the guest’s feelings: “I understand how frustrating that must have been.”

stops.name: Apologize
stops.text: Offer a **sincere, professional apology** for the inconvenience caused.

stops.name: Resolve
stops.text: Propose a way to resolve it, make sure the guest **agrees with the plan**, and offer immediate **service recovery**: a replacement item, a complimentary upgrade or loyalty points.

stops.name: Note
stops.text: Note it and follow up. **Report it to your supervisor immediately**, even if you resolved it yourself, and complete any reporting paperwork.

read.sayIt: I completely understand why you’d feel that way.

sections.name: Waits, wrong orders and spoiled food

keyPoints.line: for their patience when the wait runs long.

spoiled or inedible food, and replace it.
managers inspect it after spoiled food.

read.bigIdea: Apologize, fix it, bring in a manager.
read.where: Resolutions for the issues that come up most. In every one, **a manager is part of the fix**.

stops.name: Extended wait time
stops.text: Sincerely **apologize**, **thank the guest for their patience**, and if applicable, coordinate with a manager to offer a **complimentary soup or salad, appetizer or beverage**.

stops.name: Incorrectly filled order
stops.text: Apologize, **replace it with the correct order immediately**, and work with the manager to offer a complimentary soup or salad, appetizer or beverage.

stops.name: Spoiled or inedible food
stops.text: Offer to **replace the item immediately** and **comp it**. **Notify managers immediately** so they can inspect the remaining food on the line and prevent further issues.

sections.name: Spills, dirty tables and poor service

keyPoints.line: dry and wet, right away, after a spill.
for pointing out a dirty table or restroom.
takes the cleanup if you’re mid-service.
steps in when a guest reports poor service.

read.bigIdea: Show genuine care, then get help.
read.where: Three more, with the same rule: **notify your supervisor or manager**.

stops.name: Spilling food or drink on a guest
stops.text: Sincerely apologize, **immediately bring dry and wet towels** to limit the damage, show genuine care, and **notify your supervisor immediately** to help resolve it.

stops.name: Dirty table or restroom
stops.text: Apologize, **thank the guest** for pointing it out, and **clean and sanitize** the area immediately, or **notify the support team** if you are in the middle of active service.

stops.name: Poor service or an impolite server
stops.text: Promise to **get your manager involved immediately**, and report it so they can step in and make things right.

sources: Hospitality 101 Training, page 4: Guest conflict and problem resolution.

cards.q: What does the N in L.E.A.R.N. ask you to do?
cards.answer: Report it to your supervisor, even if you fixed it
wrong: Negotiate a discount
Nothing more once the guest is happy
Notify the rest of the guest’s party

cards.q: A guest is raising their voice. While you listen, you…
cards.answer: Stay calm and avoid matching their energy
wrong: Match their energy so they know you care
Explain the kitchen’s side right away
Walk away until they calm down

cards.q: In Resolve, before you act on a plan, you make sure…
cards.answer: The guest agrees with the plan
wrong: The kitchen agrees it was their fault
The bill has been paid
The other guests didn’t notice

cards.q: Who should hear about every guest complaint?
wrong: Only the server who handled it
No one, if it was resolved
The host stand

cards.q: What can a successfully resolved complaint build?
wrong: A longer wait list
A lower check average
A free meal for every visit

cards.q: A table has waited far too long. What do you do?
cards.answer: Apologize, thank them for their patience, and work with a manager on a complimentary item
wrong: Explain the kitchen is busy tonight
Take something off the bill on your own
Avoid the table until the food is ready

cards.q: A guest is served spoiled food. Why notify managers immediately?
cards.answer: So they can inspect the remaining food on the line
wrong: So they can lower the bill
So they can call the supplier first
So they can write up the cook

cards.q: What happens to a spoiled or inedible item?
cards.answer: It’s replaced right away and comped
wrong: It’s replaced and charged as normal
It comes off the menu for the week
The guest picks a dessert instead

cards.q: You spill a drink on a guest. What do you bring right away?
wrong: The check
A new menu
A manager’s business card

cards.q: A guest says the restroom is dirty and you’re in the middle of service. You…
cards.answer: Apologize, thank them, and notify the support team
wrong: Say someone will get to it later
Finish your tables first, then clean it
Ask them to use another restroom

cards.q: A guest complains that their server was impolite. What do you promise?
cards.answer: To get your manager involved immediately
wrong: To talk to the server yourself
To move them to another section
To take dessert off the bill
